messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Malayalam, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Malayalam line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
കവി ഞാൻ ആയിരുന്നു, ആ നീതിയുള്ളവനെക്കുറിച്ച് ഞാൻ പാടി അങ്കിസിന്റെ മകൻ, ട്രോയി നിന്നു വന്നവൻ, അഭിമാനിയായ ഇലിയോൺ കത്തിക്കപ്പെട്ടതിന് ശേഷം.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Alignment Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition (truth‑conditions) | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation (English) | Status | |-------------|------------------------------------------|----------------------|----------------------------|--------| | Poeta | speaker is a poet (identity) | കവി | “poet” | OK | | fui | speaker *was* (past copula) | ഞാൻ ആയിരുന്നു | “I was” | OK | | , | clause separator | , | “,” | OK | | e | coordinates two clauses (and) | — | — | UNNECESSARY | | cantai | speaker *sang* (past) about X | ഞാൻ പാടി | “I sang” | OK | | di | introduces object of singing (about/of) | കുറിച്ച് | “about” | OK | | quel | demonstrative “that” | ആ | “that” | OK | | giusto | property *just* of the referent | നീതിയുള്ള | “just” | OK | | figliuol | son of Anchises (parent‑child) | മകൻ | “son” | OK | | d'Anchise | genitive relation “of Anchises” | അങ്കിസിന്റെ | “of Anchises” | OK | | che (relative) | introduces relative clause “who …” | — | — | UNNECESSARY | | venne | came (motion from source) | വന്നവൻ | “who came” | OK | | di (second) | source preposition “from” | നിന്നു | “from” | OK | | Troia | city of origin “Troy” | ട്രോയി | “Troy” | OK | | , (after Troia) | clause separator | , | “,” | OK | | poi | temporal adverb “after” | ശേഷം | “after” | OK | | che (subordinator) | introduces result clause | — | — | UNNECESSARY | | 'l | definite article “the” | — | — | UNNECESSARY | | superbo | attribute “proud” of Ilion | അഭിമാനിയായ | “proud” | OK | | Ilïón | proper name “Ilion” | ഇലിയോൺ | “Ilion” | OK | | fu | auxiliary verb for passive perfect | — | — | UNNECESSARY | | combusto | passive event “was burned” | കത്തിക്കപ്പെട്ടതിന് | “having been burned” | OK | | . | sentence terminator | . | “.” | OK |
---
### Items flagged
- **UNNECESSARY**: e, che (relative), che (subordinator), 'l, fu – these function words or articles are naturally omitted in Malayalam and therefore have no direct lexical counterpart in the translation.
- **MISSING / WRONG / GRAMMAR**: none.
All other source tokens are faithfully rendered in the Malayalam output with correct meaning and grammatical agreement.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Malayalam script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Malayalam text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- Line 73: - Original: കവി ഞാൻ ആയിരുന്നു, ആ നീതിയുള്ളവനെക്കുറിച്ച് ഞാൻ പാടി - Issue: Internal comma after “ആയിരുന്നു” (source line has no end punctuation). - Corrected: കവി ഞാൻ ആയിരുന്നു ആ നീതിയുള്ളവനെക്കുറിച്ച് ഞാൻ പാടി
